header.headline: Open landing, private product
header.subhead: The code that runs this site is dual-licensed. The security product itself is commercial and stays private until you are under agreement.

dualLicense.title: Dual license: MIT / Apache-2.0
dualLicense.body: Choose the license that fits your organisation's policy. Both grants apply to the same public repository; you pick one when you use the code.

table.bestFor: Individuals, prototypes, teams that want the lightest possible license header and are not policy-bound to patent clauses.
table.considerations: No explicit patent grant. Attribution required.

table.grant: Permissive with an explicit patent grant and clearer NOTICE obligations.
table.bestFor: Companies and public-sector bodies whose legal review prefers an express patent grant and trademark/notice clarity.
table.considerations: Slightly longer obligations (NOTICE, changes declaration). Attribution required.

whichForWhom.recommendation: MIT for fastest adoption; Apache-2.0 if your default corporate standard requires a patent grant.
Apache-2.0 is usually the simpler path through procurement.
The dual grant shows the public surface is genuinely open; the product IP remains with the company.

commercial.title: Using the product commercially
commercial.body: The open licenses cover the landing repository only. To deploy Sibernetick in your environment, run a pilot, or embed it in your service portfolio, you need a commercial agreement with us.

earlyAccess.title: Early access
earlyAccess.body: Design partners evaluate the product under agreement before general availability. Early access includes direct engineering contact and influence over the roadmap.
